sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File header and imports
sections.what: Explains that this file reads research replies for new projects and reuses the closure loader's helpers.
sections.why: Reuse keeps claim extraction the same for new and existing projects.
sections.watch_out: Changes to the reused helpers in closureReplies.ts also change this file's behaviour.

sections.name: PopulationBlock
sections.title: The parsed block shape
sections.what: Describes the parts of one parsed reply: the file, its fingerprint, the producer, the worklist id, leftover items, suggested candidates and project list.
sections.why: Gives the importer a single structure to work from.
sections.watch_out: Missing lists are replaced with empty lists rather than causing an error.

sections.name: parsePopulationFile
sections.title: Reading one reply file
sections.what: Reads a file, removes chat markers, splits out each JSON object and checks each one. Stops with a clear error if any object is invalid or is not a population reply.
sections.why: Rejects malformed model output early, before it can reach the database.
sections.watch_out: The producer name is lowercased here, so other code must use the same casing.

sections.name: populationPlannerRecord
sections.title: Converting a project record
sections.what: Turns one project record into the shape the planner expects: trims the key, renames company and scope fields, and merges delivery facts into the facts list.
sections.why: Lets population records use the same planner as existing projects.
sections.watch_out: A record without a project key stops the run with an error naming the project.

summary: Reads population-style research reply files and turns each project record into the shape the shared planner expects.
purpose: Lets research replies for new projects, keyed by fixed project keys, be processed by the same claim-extraction code used for existing projects.
why: The header says it reuses the closure loader so both paths extract claims the same way.
how: 1. Reads the file and cleans out chat marker text. 2. Splits the text into JSON objects. 3. Checks each object is a population reply with a producer, worklist id and project list. 4. Returns one block per object. 5. Converts each project into the planner shape, renaming company and scope fields and merging delivery facts into facts.
inputs: A reply file name and its raw text, from an AI researcher.
outputs: A list of parsed blocks with the file, a fingerprint of the file, the producer, the worklist id, leftover items, suggested candidates and project records.
risks: Relies on helper code in closureReplies.ts. A change there changes this importer. Producer names are lowercased, which could mismatch if other code expects different casing.
debug: If a file is rejected, the error names the file and the object number. Check that the object has schema yard-research/1 and mode population, and that producer, worklist_id and projects are present. A project without a project_key throws an error that names the project.
